title: To the rescue: Feline Connection cares for local cat population | Local News | rutlandherald.com
text:
They have names like Peach Cobbler, Sassy, and Pete the Cat. Two foster kittens’ names had a slang theme — Dealio and Jeez Louise.
“It’s so we can put them in our database and have a name to identify them,” said volunteer Robin Burgart.
Last Saturday, there were kittens in every corner of Phoenix Books when the Feline Connection brought some of their adoptable rescue cats for a meet and greet.
The local nonprofit has rescued hundreds of stray and feral cats, and kittens to spay and neuter them to keep the population down, and find good homes for the kittens. They rely entirely on donations and volunteers, a group of whom foster the cats in their own homes until they’re adopted because the Feline Connection does not have a brick-and-mortar location.
Burgart has been fostering and volunteering for two years. It started when she noticed a stray cat left behind by her neighbors.
“We watched her have a couple litters,” she said. “We caught her to spay her, and I had never dealt with a feral cat before so I contacted Diane, our main trapper, who had helped our neighbor across the street with kittens in his garage.”
In that neighborhood alone, Burgart said dozens of strays have been rescued.
“If they’re truly feral, they’re going to be the happiest where they came from,” Burgart said. “We get them spayed or neutered and release them back to their area (and) clip or notch the left ear so when we’re looking we can see who we did, and we have it in our database.”
The pregnant cat that got Burgart involved with Feline Connection was feral and brought back to the neighborhood in which she was found, but now she’s up to date on shots and properly spayed.
“You can’t touch her, but she knows she’s loved,” Burgart said. “She’s well taken care of, and she’s not having kittens anymore.”
Her litter was fostered by volunteers and adopted out, and the meet and greets have been a great way to do that. Two kitties called Sugar and Spice were adopted at a Tractor Supply event a couple weeks ago, and their new owners wrote in, “We’re so happy we adopted them. They were definitely what we needed in our home.”
“We are committed to finding each cat a safe and healthy permanent home,” the Feline Connection website says. “We work to find the best possible home matches for each of our stray or friendly ‘colony cats’ based on their unique needs, as well as the adopter’s needs.”
Kirsten Davenport, vice president, secretary and social media coordinator for Feline Connection, said the organization has two upcoming events: From 2 to 5 p.m. Friday, Oct. 3, at the West Rutland Library, and a basket raffle at the Castleton Legion at 11 a.m. on Sunday, Oct. 26.
“We are looking for volunteers, basket donations and certificate donations. People can contact info@thefelineconnection.org,” she added.
Burgart said at the last meet and greet, four kittens were adopted. “They had to be spayed and neutered, and that was on the 23rd and they went home on Aug. 30.”
“Jeez Louise is going home to a 6-year-old who has been waiting as we finished her shot series,” Burgart said. “He took her bowl to show-and-tell at school, he’s so excited, he’s got her room ready, he put her perch together, he’s got toys for her, he’s got a carrier for her. It just warms my heart. That’s what it’s about.”
Learn more at www.thefelineconnection.org.
